name: Acquired Motor Neuron Disease

criteria.description: Presence of upper motor neuron signs in at least one region
Presence of lower motor neuron signs in at least one region
Progressive spread of symptoms or signs within a region or to other regions
Exclusion of other diseases that can explain symptoms

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of combined upper and lower motor neuron signs with progressive spread and exclusion of alternative diagnoses
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical supported by electromyography and neuroimaging to exclude mimics.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Progressive muscle weakness with both upper and lower motor neuron signs
searchTerms: progressive muscle weakness upper and lower neurons
weak muscles with nerve damage signs
combined upper and lower motor neuron weakness

pathognomonic.symptomName: Muscle atrophy due to lower motor neuron degeneration
searchTerms: muscle shrinkage due to nerve damage
atrophy caused by lower motor neuron loss

pathognomonic.symptomName: Spasticity reflecting upper motor neuron involvement
searchTerms: muscle stiffness from upper motor neuron

common.symptomName: Dysarthria due to bulbar motor neuron involvement
searchTerms: slurred speech from brainstem nerve damage
difficulty speaking due to bulbar weakness
speech problems from motor neuron involvement
difficulty swallowing from weak throat muscles
swallowing problems due to bulbar weakness

occasional.symptomName: Mild cognitive impairment or frontotemporal dysfunction
Respiratory muscle weakness leading to dyspnea on exertion
searchTerms: weak breathing muscles causing shortness of breath

occasional.symptomName: Weight loss due to muscle wasting
searchTerms: losing weight due to muscle loss

rare.notes: Rarely observed in typical acquired motor neuron disease

rare.symptomName: Sensory symptoms such as numbness or paresthesia
rare.notes: Usually absent, presence suggests alternative diagnosis

rare.symptomName: Severe respiratory failure requiring mechanical ventilation early in disease

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests; exclusion of metabolic or inflammatory causes
Elevated neurofilament light chain in CSF or serum (research setting)
imaging: MRI brain and spinal cord to exclude structural lesions or alternative diagnoses
Electromyography showing denervation and reinnervation patterns
genetic: Usually sporadic; genetic testing may be performed to exclude hereditary motor neuron diseases
other: Pulmonary function tests to assess respiratory muscle involvement

distinguishingFeatures: Genetic testing positive for known mutations
Presence of conduction block on nerve conduction studies

redFlags: Rapidly progressive weakness with sensory loss
Presence of autonomic dysfunction or prominent sensory symptoms
references: Brooks BR. El Escorial World Federation of Neurology criteria for the diagnosis of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis. J Neurol Sci. 1994.
Hardiman O, et al. Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis. Nat Rev Dis Primers. 2017.
Orphanet: Acquired Motor Neuron Disease. ORPHA:98506.
